title: MD SB8: Criminal Law - Identity Fraud - Artificial Intelligence and Deepfake Representations

prohibitions: A person may not knowingly, willfully, and with fraudulent intent possess, obtain, or help another to possess or obtain any personal identifying information of an individual, without the consent of the individual, in order to use, sell, or transfer the information to get a benefit, credit, good, service, or other thing of value or to access health information or health care (§ 8-301(b))

A person may not maliciously use an interactive computer service to disclose or assist another person to disclose the driver's license number, bank or other financial institution account number, credit card number, payment device number, Social Security number, or employee identification number of an individual, without the consent of the individual, in order to annoy, threaten, embarrass, or harass the individual (§ 8-301(b-1))

A person may not knowingly, willfully, and with fraudulent intent utilize the personal identifying information of an individual, without the consent of the individual, in order to cause harm (§ 8-301(b-2))

A person may not knowingly and willfully assume the identity of another, including a fictitious person, to avoid identification, apprehension, or prosecution for a crime, or with fraudulent intent to get a benefit, credit, good, service, or other thing of value, access health information or health care, avoid the payment of debt or other legal obligation, or harm, harass, intimidate, threaten, or coerce the other person (§ 8-301(c))

A person may not knowingly, willfully, and with fraudulent intent to obtain a benefit, credit, good, service, or other thing of value or to access health information or health care, use a re encoder to place information encoded on the magnetic strip or stripe of a credit card onto the magnetic strip or stripe of a different credit card or use any other electronic medium that allows such a transaction to occur without the consent of the individual authorized to use the credit card from which the personal identifying information or payment device number is being re encoded, or use a skimming device to access, read, scan, obtain, memorize, or store personal identifying information or a payment device number on the magnetic strip or stripe of a credit card without the consent of the individual authorized to use the credit card (§ 8-301(d))

A person may not knowingly, willfully, and with fraudulent intent possess, obtain, or help another possess or obtain a re encoder device or a skimming device for the unauthorized use, sale, or transfer of personal identifying information or a payment device number (§ 8-301(e))

A person may not knowingly and willfully claim to represent another person without the knowledge and consent of that person, with the intent to solicit, request, or take any other action to otherwise induce another person to provide personal identifying information or a payment device number (§ 8-301(f)(1))

A person may not knowingly, willfully, and with fraudulent intent use artificial intelligence or a deepfake representation to impersonate, falsely depict, or claim to represent another person with the intent to defraud, mislead, or cause harm to that person or any other person cause harm to another by impersonating, falsely depicting, or claiming to represent that person or any other person, or to create or distribute false records with the intent to cause harm to another person, induce another person to provide personal identifying information, or obtain a benefit, credit, good, service, or other thing of value (§ 8-301(f)(2))
reading.what_it_does: Amends Maryland's identity fraud statute to prohibit using personal identifying information without consent to cause harm, and to prohibit using artificial intelligence or deepfake representations to impersonate, falsely depict, or claim to represent another person with fraudulent intent, or to create or distribute false records to cause harm, induce disclosure of personal identifying information, or obtain a benefit. It establishes criminal penalties and a private civil action for victims of AI or deepfake violations.
key_definitions: Artificial intelligence: a machine-based system that can, for a given set of human-defined objectives, make predictions, recommendations, or decisions influencing real or virtual environments; uses machine and human-based inputs to perceive real and virtual environments and abstracts those perceptions into models through analysis in an automated manner; and uses model inference to formulate options for information or action (§ 3.5-801(c), State Finance and Procurement Article, as incorporated by § 8-301(a)(2))

Deepfake representation: a photograph, a film, a video, an audio recording, a digital image, a picture, or a computer or computer-generated image or picture, whether made, produced, or generated by electronic, mechanical, or other means, that is indistinguishable from an actual and identifiable human being; does not include images or items depicting human beings that are drawings, cartoons, sculptures, or paintings (§ 8-301(a)(3))
Harm: physical injury; serious emotional distress; or economic damages (§ 8-301(a)(4))

Indistinguishable from an actual and identifiable human being: an image an ordinary person would conclude is of an actual and identifiable human being; includes an image that is computer-generated and has been created, adapted, or modified to appear as an actual and identifiable human being (§ 8-301(a)(7))

Personal identifying information: includes a name, address, telephone number, driver's license number, Social Security number, place of employment, employee identification number, health insurance identification number, medical identification number, mother's maiden name, bank or other financial institution account number, date of birth, personal identification number, unique biometric data, including fingerprint, voice print, retina or iris image or other unique physical representation, digital signature, credit card number, or other payment device number; may be derived from any element alone or in conjunction with any other information to identify a specific natural or fictitious individual (§ 8-301(a)(10))

Health care: care, services, or supplies related to the health of an individual that includes preventative, diagnostic, therapeutic, rehabilitative, maintenance care, palliative care and counseling, service assessment, or procedure with respect to the physical or mental condition or functional status of an individual or that affects the structure or function of the body; and the sale or dispensing of a drug, device, equipment, or other item in accordance with a prescription (§ 8-301(a)(5))

Health information: any information, whether oral or recorded in any form or medium, that is created or received by a health care provider, health care carrier, public health authority, employer, life insurer, school or university, or health care clearinghouse; and relates to the past, present, or future physical or mental health or condition of an individual, the provision of health care to an individual, or the past, present, or future payment for the provision of health care to an individual (§ 8-301(a)(6))

Interactive computer service: an information service, system, or access software provider that provides or enables computer access by multiple users to a computer server, including a system that provides access to the Internet and cellular phones (§ 8-301(a)(8))
Payment device number: has the meaning stated in § 8-213 of this title (§ 8-301(a)(9))

Re-encoder: an electronic device that places encoded personal identifying information or a payment device number from the magnetic strip or stripe of a credit card onto the magnetic strip or stripe of a different credit card or any electronic medium that allows such a transaction to occur (§ 8-301(a)(11))

Skimming device: a scanner, skimmer, reader, or any other electronic device that is used to access, read, scan, obtain, memorize, or store, temporarily or permanently, personal identifying information or a payment device number encoded on the magnetic strip or stripe of a credit card (§ 8-301(a)(12))
who_it_applies_to: Any person, as the statute uses 'a person' without limitation (Section 8-301)
notable_exemptions: The definition of deepfake representation does not include images or items depicting human beings that are drawings, cartoons, sculptures, or paintings (§ 8-301(a)(3)(II))
reading.penalties_and_enforcement: The Department of State Police may initiate investigations and enforce this section throughout the State without regard to any limitation otherwise applicable to the Department's activities in a municipal corporation or other political subdivision (§ 8-301(l)). Other law enforcement officers of specified agencies may investigate violations statewide in accordance with regulations adopted by the Department of State Police (§ 8-301(m)). A State's Attorney or the Attorney General may investigate and prosecute a violation (§ 8-301(p)). Prosecution may be commenced in any county where an element of the crime occurred or where the victim resides (§ 8-301(q)). Criminal penalties vary by subsection and value: violations of (b), (c)(2)(i)-(iii), or (d) with value at least $1,500 but less than $25,000 are a felony with imprisonment up to 5 years or fine up to $10,000 or both; at least $25,000 but less than $100,000 are a felony with imprisonment up to 10 years or fine up to $15,000 or both; $100,000 or more are a felony with imprisonment up to 20 years or fine up to $25,000 or both; at least $100 but less than $1,500 are a misdemeanor with imprisonment up to 1 year or fine up to $500 or both (§ 8-301(g)(1)-(2)). Violations of (b-1), (b-2), (c)(1), (c)(2)(iv), (e), or (f)(1) are a misdemeanor with imprisonment up to 1 year or fine up to $500 or both (§ 8-301(g)(4)). Violations of (f)(2) involving one victim are a felony with imprisonment up to 5 years or fine up to $10,000 or both; involving two or more victims are a felony with imprisonment up to 10 years or fine up to $15,000 or both (§ 8-301(g)(5)). A person who violates this section under circumstances reasonably indicating intent to manufacture, distribute, or dispense another individual's personal identifying information without consent is guilty of a felony with imprisonment up to 10 years or fine up to $25,000 or both (§ 8-301(g)(3)). When the violation is pursuant to one scheme or continuing course of conduct, the conduct may be considered as one violation and the value may be aggregated (§ 8-301(g)(6)). A court may order restitution for reasonable costs including attorney's fees for clearing credit history, clearing health information records, and civil or administrative proceedings to satisfy debts arising from the violation (§ 8-301(j)). A victim of an act that would constitute a violation of (f)(2) may bring a civil action against the person or persons who committed the act; the court may issue an injunction to prevent or restrain an act that would constitute a violation of (f)(2) and grant any other appropriate relief (§ 8-301(h)).
how_it_affects_ai_deployment: An organisation that uses artificial intelligence or a deepfake representation to impersonate, falsely depict, or claim to represent another person with fraudulent intent, or to create or distribute false records to cause harm, induce disclosure of personal identifying information, or obtain a benefit, commits a felony punishable by up to 5 years imprisonment or a $10,000 fine for one victim, or up to 10 years imprisonment or a $15,000 fine for two or more victims (§ 8-301(f)(2), § 8-301(g)(5))
A victim of such AI or deepfake misuse may bring a civil action against the organisation, and a court may issue an injunction and grant other appropriate relief (§ 8-301(h))
Using personal identifying information without consent to cause harm, even without AI, is a misdemeanor punishable by up to 1 year imprisonment or a $500 fine (§ 8-301(b-2), § 8-301(g)(4))

The organisation may be subject to investigation and prosecution by the Department of State Police, other designated law enforcement agencies, a State's Attorney, or the Attorney General, and prosecution may be brought in any county where an element occurred or where the victim resides (§ 8-301(l), § 8-301(m), § 8-301(p), § 8-301(q))
There is no exemption for commercial or organisational use of AI or deepfakes; the statute applies to any person (§ 8-301(f)(2))

What it does

Amends Maryland's identity fraud statute to prohibit using personal identifying information without consent to cause harm, and to prohibit using artificial intelligence or deepfake representations to impersonate, falsely depict, or claim to represent another person with fraudulent intent, or to create or distribute false records to cause harm, induce disclosure of personal identifying information, or obtain a benefit. It establishes criminal penalties and a private civil action for victims of AI or deepfake violations.

Who it applies to

  • Any person, as the statute uses 'a person' without limitation (Section 8-301)

Effective date

October 1, 2026 (Section 2)

Key definitions

  • Artificial intelligence: a machine-based system that can, for a given set of human-defined objectives, make predictions, recommendations, or decisions influencing real or virtual environments; uses machine and human-based inputs to perceive real and virtual environments and abstracts those perceptions into models through analysis in an automated manner; and uses model inference to formulate options for information or action (§ 3.5-801(c), State Finance and Procurement Article, as incorporated by § 8-301(a)(2))
  • Deepfake representation: a photograph, a film, a video, an audio recording, a digital image, a picture, or a computer or computer-generated image or picture, whether made, produced, or generated by electronic, mechanical, or other means, that is indistinguishable from an actual and identifiable human being; does not include images or items depicting human beings that are drawings, cartoons, sculptures, or paintings (§ 8-301(a)(3))
  • Harm: physical injury; serious emotional distress; or economic damages (§ 8-301(a)(4))
  • Indistinguishable from an actual and identifiable human being: an image an ordinary person would conclude is of an actual and identifiable human being; includes an image that is computer-generated and has been created, adapted, or modified to appear as an actual and identifiable human being (§ 8-301(a)(7))
  • Personal identifying information: includes a name, address, telephone number, driver's license number, Social Security number, place of employment, employee identification number, health insurance identification number, medical identification number, mother's maiden name, bank or other financial institution account number, date of birth, personal identification number, unique biometric data, including fingerprint, voice print, retina or iris image or other unique physical representation, digital signature, credit card number, or other payment device number; may be derived from any element alone or in conjunction with any other information to identify a specific natural or fictitious individual (§ 8-301(a)(10))
  • Health care: care, services, or supplies related to the health of an individual that includes preventative, diagnostic, therapeutic, rehabilitative, maintenance care, palliative care and counseling, service assessment, or procedure with respect to the physical or mental condition or functional status of an individual or that affects the structure or function of the body; and the sale or dispensing of a drug, device, equipment, or other item in accordance with a prescription (§ 8-301(a)(5))
  • Health information: any information, whether oral or recorded in any form or medium, that is created or received by a health care provider, health care carrier, public health authority, employer, life insurer, school or university, or health care clearinghouse; and relates to the past, present, or future physical or mental health or condition of an individual, the provision of health care to an individual, or the past, present, or future payment for the provision of health care to an individual (§ 8-301(a)(6))
  • Interactive computer service: an information service, system, or access software provider that provides or enables computer access by multiple users to a computer server, including a system that provides access to the Internet and cellular phones (§ 8-301(a)(8))
  • Payment device number: has the meaning stated in § 8-213 of this title (§ 8-301(a)(9))
  • Re-encoder: an electronic device that places encoded personal identifying information or a payment device number from the magnetic strip or stripe of a credit card onto the magnetic strip or stripe of a different credit card or any electronic medium that allows such a transaction to occur (§ 8-301(a)(11))
  • Skimming device: a scanner, skimmer, reader, or any other electronic device that is used to access, read, scan, obtain, memorize, or store, temporarily or permanently, personal identifying information or a payment device number encoded on the magnetic strip or stripe of a credit card (§ 8-301(a)(12))

Obligations

  • not stated in the text

Prohibitions

  • A person may not knowingly, willfully, and with fraudulent intent possess, obtain, or help another to possess or obtain any personal identifying information of an individual, without the consent of the individual, in order to use, sell, or transfer the information to get a benefit, credit, good, service, or other thing of value or to access health information or health care (§ 8-301(b))
  • A person may not maliciously use an interactive computer service to disclose or assist another person to disclose the driver's license number, bank or other financial institution account number, credit card number, payment device number, Social Security number, or employee identification number of an individual, without the consent of the individual, in order to annoy, threaten, embarrass, or harass the individual (§ 8-301(b-1))
  • A person may not knowingly, willfully, and with fraudulent intent utilize the personal identifying information of an individual, without the consent of the individual, in order to cause harm (§ 8-301(b-2))
  • A person may not knowingly and willfully assume the identity of another, including a fictitious person, to avoid identification, apprehension, or prosecution for a crime, or with fraudulent intent to get a benefit, credit, good, service, or other thing of value, access health information or health care, avoid the payment of debt or other legal obligation, or harm, harass, intimidate, threaten, or coerce the other person (§ 8-301(c))
  • A person may not knowingly, willfully, and with fraudulent intent to obtain a benefit, credit, good, service, or other thing of value or to access health information or health care, use a re encoder to place information encoded on the magnetic strip or stripe of a credit card onto the magnetic strip or stripe of a different credit card or use any other electronic medium that allows such a transaction to occur without the consent of the individual authorized to use the credit card from which the personal identifying information or payment device number is being re encoded, or use a skimming device to access, read, scan, obtain, memorize, or store personal identifying information or a payment device number on the magnetic strip or stripe of a credit card without the consent of the individual authorized to use the credit card (§ 8-301(d))
  • A person may not knowingly, willfully, and with fraudulent intent possess, obtain, or help another possess or obtain a re encoder device or a skimming device for the unauthorized use, sale, or transfer of personal identifying information or a payment device number (§ 8-301(e))
  • A person may not knowingly and willfully claim to represent another person without the knowledge and consent of that person, with the intent to solicit, request, or take any other action to otherwise induce another person to provide personal identifying information or a payment device number (§ 8-301(f)(1))
  • A person may not knowingly, willfully, and with fraudulent intent use artificial intelligence or a deepfake representation to impersonate, falsely depict, or claim to represent another person with the intent to defraud, mislead, or cause harm to that person or any other person cause harm to another by impersonating, falsely depicting, or claiming to represent that person or any other person, or to create or distribute false records with the intent to cause harm to another person, induce another person to provide personal identifying information, or obtain a benefit, credit, good, service, or other thing of value (§ 8-301(f)(2))

Penalties and enforcement

The Department of State Police may initiate investigations and enforce this section throughout the State without regard to any limitation otherwise applicable to the Department's activities in a municipal corporation or other political subdivision (§ 8-301(l)). Other law enforcement officers of specified agencies may investigate violations statewide in accordance with regulations adopted by the Department of State Police (§ 8-301(m)). A State's Attorney or the Attorney General may investigate and prosecute a violation (§ 8-301(p)). Prosecution may be commenced in any county where an element of the crime occurred or where the victim resides (§ 8-301(q)). Criminal penalties vary by subsection and value: violations of (b), (c)(2)(i)-(iii), or (d) with value at least $1,500 but less than $25,000 are a felony with imprisonment up to 5 years or fine up to $10,000 or both; at least $25,000 but less than $100,000 are a felony with imprisonment up to 10 years or fine up to $15,000 or both; $100,000 or more are a felony with imprisonment up to 20 years or fine up to $25,000 or both; at least $100 but less than $1,500 are a misdemeanor with imprisonment up to 1 year or fine up to $500 or both (§ 8-301(g)(1)-(2)). Violations of (b-1), (b-2), (c)(1), (c)(2)(iv), (e), or (f)(1) are a misdemeanor with imprisonment up to 1 year or fine up to $500 or both (§ 8-301(g)(4)). Violations of (f)(2) involving one victim are a felony with imprisonment up to 5 years or fine up to $10,000 or both; involving two or more victims are a felony with imprisonment up to 10 years or fine up to $15,000 or both (§ 8-301(g)(5)). A person who violates this section under circumstances reasonably indicating intent to manufacture, distribute, or dispense another individual's personal identifying information without consent is guilty of a felony with imprisonment up to 10 years or fine up to $25,000 or both (§ 8-301(g)(3)). When the violation is pursuant to one scheme or continuing course of conduct, the conduct may be considered as one violation and the value may be aggregated (§ 8-301(g)(6)). A court may order restitution for reasonable costs including attorney's fees for clearing credit history, clearing health information records, and civil or administrative proceedings to satisfy debts arising from the violation (§ 8-301(j)). A victim of an act that would constitute a violation of (f)(2) may bring a civil action against the person or persons who committed the act; the court may issue an injunction to prevent or restrain an act that would constitute a violation of (f)(2) and grant any other appropriate relief (§ 8-301(h)).

How it affects AI deployment

  • An organisation that uses artificial intelligence or a deepfake representation to impersonate, falsely depict, or claim to represent another person with fraudulent intent, or to create or distribute false records to cause harm, induce disclosure of personal identifying information, or obtain a benefit, commits a felony punishable by up to 5 years imprisonment or a $10,000 fine for one victim, or up to 10 years imprisonment or a $15,000 fine for two or more victims (§ 8-301(f)(2), § 8-301(g)(5))
  • A victim of such AI or deepfake misuse may bring a civil action against the organisation, and a court may issue an injunction and grant other appropriate relief (§ 8-301(h))
  • Using personal identifying information without consent to cause harm, even without AI, is a misdemeanor punishable by up to 1 year imprisonment or a $500 fine (§ 8-301(b-2), § 8-301(g)(4))
  • The organisation may be subject to investigation and prosecution by the Department of State Police, other designated law enforcement agencies, a State's Attorney, or the Attorney General, and prosecution may be brought in any county where an element occurred or where the victim resides (§ 8-301(l), § 8-301(m), § 8-301(p), § 8-301(q))
  • There is no exemption for commercial or organisational use of AI or deepfakes; the statute applies to any person (§ 8-301(f)(2))

Notable exemptions

  • The definition of deepfake representation does not include images or items depicting human beings that are drawings, cartoons, sculptures, or paintings (§ 8-301(a)(3)(II))

Compliance steps

  • not stated in the text
